title: 'The Open Boat' by Stephen Crane, Part Two
titleZh: 《海上扁舟》,史蒂芬·克莱恩著,第二部分

sentences.en: We continue the story of “The Open Boat” by Stephen Crane.
sentences.zh: 我们继续讲述斯蒂芬·克莱恩的《敞开的船》的故事。

sentences.en: As we told you last week, the story is based on true events.
sentences.zh: 正如上周我们所讲，这个故事是基于真实事件改编的。

sentences.en: In eighteen ninety-six, Crane was traveling to Cuba as a news reporter.
sentences.zh: 1896年，克莱恩作为新闻记者前往古巴。

sentences.en: On his way there, his ship sank in the Atlantic Ocean.
sentences.zh: 在前往那里的途中，他的船在大西洋沉没了。

sentences.en: Crane climbed into the last remaining lifeboat.
sentences.zh: 克莱恩爬进了最后剩下的救生艇。

sentences.en: Three men got into the boat with him.
sentences.zh: 有三个男人和他一起上了艇。

sentences.en: They were the ship’s captain, the cook and a sailor named Billie.
sentences.zh: 他们是船上的船长、厨师和一位名叫比利的水手。

sentences.en: For three days, the men steered the small boat through high waves along the coast of Florida.
sentences.zh: 三天里，男人们驾驶着这艘小船，沿着佛罗里达海岸穿越汹涌的巨浪。

sentences.en: At last, they saw land.
sentences.zh: 终于，他们看到了陆地。

sentences.en: Here is Shep O’Neal with the final part of the story.
sentences.zh: 以下是谢普·奥尼尔带来的故事的最后部分。

sentences.en: A long stretch of coast lay before the eyes of the men.
sentences.zh: 一片漫长的海岸展现在男人们眼前。

sentences.en: Slowly, the land rose up out of the mountainous sea.
sentences.zh: 慢慢地，陆地从如群山般起伏的海面上升起。

sentences.en: The men could see a small house against the sky.
sentences.zh: 男人们能看到一座小房子矗立在天空之下。

sentences.en: To the south, they could see a lighthouse.
sentences.zh: 往南，他们能看到一座灯塔。

sentences.en: Tide, wind and waves were pushing the lifeboat northward.
sentences.zh: 潮水、风和波浪正把救生艇向北推去。

sentences.en: The men thought someone on land would have seen the boat by now.
sentences.zh: 男人们认为岸上的人此刻应该已经看到这艘船了。

sentences.en: “Well,” said the captain, “I suppose we’ll have to attempt to reach the shore ourselves.
sentences.zh: “好吧，”船长说，“我想我们得靠自己设法靠岸了。

sentences.en: If we stay out here too long, none of us will have the strength left to swim after the boat sinks.”
sentences.zh: 如果我们在这里待得太久，等船沉了，我们谁也游不动了。”

sentences.en: So Billie the sailor turned the boat straight for the shore.
sentences.zh: 于是水手比利把船头对准了海岸。

sentences.en: “If we don’t all get ashore,” said the captain, “I suppose you fellows know where to send news of my death?”
sentences.zh: “如果我们不能全都上岸，”船长说，“我想你们这些家伙知道该往哪儿报告我的死讯吧？”

sentences.en: The men then exchanged some information.
sentences.zh: 随后，这些人交换了一些信息。

sentences.en: There was a great deal of anger in them.
sentences.zh: 他们心中充满了愤怒。

sentences.en: They thought: “If I am going to be drowned, why, in the name of the seven mad gods who rule the sea, was I permitted to come this far and think about sand and trees?”
sentences.zh: 他们想：“如果我注定要淹死，那么，以统治海洋的七个疯神的名义，我为什么被允许来到这么远的地方，却想着沙滩和树木？”

sentences.en: The waves grew stronger.
sentences.zh: 海浪变得更强了。

sentences.en: They seemed always just about to break and roll over the little boat.
sentences.zh: 它们似乎总是即将破碎并翻滚过那艘小船。

sentences.en: The coast was still far away.
sentences.zh: 海岸仍然还很遥远。

sentences.en: The sailor said: “Boys, the boat won’t live three minutes more, and we’re too far out to swim.
sentences.zh: 水手说：“孩子们，这艘船撑不过三分钟了，而我们离岸太远，游不回去。

sentences.en: Shall I take her to sea again, captain?”
sentences.zh: 我要不要把它再划回海里，船长？”

sentences.en: “Yes!
Go ahead!” said the captain.
sentences.zh: 继续划！”船长说道。

sentences.en: The sailor turned the boat and took her safely out to sea again.
sentences.zh: 水手把船转向，安全地再次把它划到了海里。

sentences.en: “It’s funny those life-saving people haven’t seen us,” one of the men said.
sentences.zh: “真有趣，那些救生的人竟然没看到我们，”其中一个人说道。

sentences.en: “Maybe they think we’re out here for sport!
sentences.zh: “也许他们认为我们是在这里为了消遣！

sentences.en: Maybe they think we’re fishing.
sentences.zh: 也许他们认为我们在钓鱼。

sentences.en: Maybe they think we’re fools.”
sentences.zh: 也许他们认为我们是傻瓜。”

sentences.en: Once more, the sailor rowed the boat and then the reporter rowed.
sentences.zh: 又一次，水手划了船，然后记者划了船。

sentences.en: Suddenly, they saw a man walking along the shore.
sentences.zh: 突然，他们看到一个人沿着海岸走来。

sentences.en: The man stopped walking.
sentences.zh: 那个人停下了脚步。

sentences.en: He moved his hand in the air to wave at them.
sentences.zh: 他在空中挥了挥手，向他们示意。

sentences.en: He saw them!
sentences.zh: 他看到他们了！

sentences.en: Now he was running to the house.
sentences.zh: 现在他正朝房子跑去。

sentences.en: The captain tied a cloth to a stick and waved it.
sentences.zh: 船长把一块布绑在棍子上，挥动着。

sentences.en: Now there was another man on the shore.
sentences.zh: 现在岸上又出现了另一个人。

sentences.en: The two men waved their hands in the air, as if they were saying hello to the men in the boat.
sentences.zh: 这两个人在空中挥着手，仿佛是在向船上的人打招呼。

sentences.en: Now, what was that moving on the shore?
sentences.zh: 那么，岸上那移动的东西是什么？

sentences.en: It was a bus – a hotel bus.
sentences.zh: 那是一辆公共汽车——一辆旅游大巴。

sentences.en: A man stood on the steps of the bus and waved his coat over his head.
sentences.zh: 一名男子站在大巴的台阶上，把外套举过头顶挥动。

sentences.en: The men in the boat wondered what he wanted to say.
sentences.zh: 船上的人想知道他想要说些什么。

sentences.en: Was he attempting to tell them something?
sentences.zh: 他是不是想告诉他们些什么？

sentences.en: Should they wait for help?
sentences.zh: 他们该留下来等救援吗？

sentences.en: Should they go north?
sentences.zh: 他们该往北去吗？

sentences.en: Should they go south?
sentences.zh: 他们该往南去吗？

sentences.en: The men waited and waited but nothing happened.
sentences.zh: 那些人等了又等，可是什么也没发生。

sentences.en: The sun began to go down.
sentences.zh: 太阳开始落山了。

sentences.en: It got dark and cold.
sentences.zh: 天渐渐黑了，也变冷了。

sentences.en: They could no longer see anyone on the beach.
sentences.zh: 他们再也看不到海滩上有任何人了。

sentences.en: The sailor rowed, and then the reporter rowed, and then the sailor rowed again.
sentences.zh: 水手划船，然后记者划船，接着水手又划起来。

sentences.en: They rowed and rowed through the long night.
sentences.zh: 他们彻夜不停地划着船。

sentences.en: The land had disappeared but they could hear the low sound of the waves hitting the shore.
sentences.zh: 陆地已经消失了，但他们仍能听到海浪轻拍岸边的低沉声响。

sentences.en: This was surely a quiet night.
sentences.zh: 这 certainly 是个宁静的夜晚。

sentences.en: The cook finally spoke: “Billie, what kind of pie do you like best?”
sentences.zh: 厨师终于开口了：“比利，你最喜欢什么馅的派？”

sentences.en: “Pie,” said the sailor and the reporter angrily.
sentences.zh: “派，”水手和记者怒气冲冲地说。

sentences.en: “Don’t talk about those things!”
sentences.zh: “别提那些东西了！”

sentences.en: “Well,” said the cook, “I was just thinking about ham sandwiches, and …”
sentences.zh: “嗯，”厨师说，“我刚才正想着火腿三明治呢，还有……”

sentences.en: A night on the sea in an open boat is a long night.
sentences.zh: 在敞口小船上度过的大海之夜，是漫长的一夜。

sentences.en: The sailor continued to row until his head fell forward and sleep overpowered him.
sentences.zh: 水手一直划船，直到脑袋垂下，睡意袭来将他淹没。

sentences.en: Then he asked the reporter to row for a while.
sentences.zh: 然后他让记者接替划船。

sentences.en: They exchanged places so the sailor could sleep in the bottom of the boat with the cook and the captain.
sentences.zh: 两人交换了位置，这样水手就能和厨师、船长一起在船底睡觉。

sentences.en: The reporter thought that he was the one man afloat on all the oceans in the world.
sentences.zh: 记者觉得自己是这世界上所有海洋上唯一活着的人。

sentences.en: The wind had a sad voice as it came over the waves.
sentences.zh: 风掠过波浪时带着悲伤的声音。

sentences.en: Suddenly, there was a long, loud swishing sound behind the boat and a shining trail of silvery blue.
sentences.zh: 忽然，船后传来一阵悠长而响亮的哗啦声，还有一道银蓝色的闪亮轨迹。

sentences.en: It might have been made by a huge knife.
sentences.zh: 那痕迹仿佛是由一把巨大的刀划出来的。

sentences.en: Then there was another swish and another long flash of bluish light, this time alongside the boat.
sentences.zh: 接着又是一阵哗啦声，又一次长长的幽蓝色闪光，这次是在船旁。

sentences.en: The reporter saw a huge fin speed like a shadow through the water, leaving a long glowing trail.
sentences.zh: 记者看见一条巨大的鱼鳍像影子一样在水中疾驰而过，留下一道长长的发光轨迹。

sentences.en: The thing kept swimming near the boat.
sentences.zh: 那东西一直在船附近游动。

sentences.en: He noted its speed and power.
sentences.zh: 他留意到了它的速度和力量。

sentences.en: The reporter wished the men would wake up.
sentences.zh: 记者希望那些人能醒过来。

sentences.en: He did not want to be alone with the shark.
sentences.zh: 他不想独自和这条鲨鱼待在一起。

sentences.en: The reporter thought as he rowed.
sentences.zh: 记者在划船时这样想着。

sentences.en: He was angry that they had come so close to land and yet might still die at sea.
sentences.zh: 他很生气，他们明明已经离陆地那么近了，却可能仍然会葬身大海。

sentences.en: Then he remembered a poem that he had learned as a child.
sentences.zh: 然后他想起了小时候学过的一首诗。

sentences.en: It was a poem about a soldier of the French Foreign Legion.
sentences.zh: 那是一首赞说法国外籍军团士兵的诗。

sentences.en: The soldier lay dying in Algiers.
sentences.zh: 那名士兵躺在阿尔及尔，生命垂危。

sentences.en: Just before he died, he cried out: “I shall never see my own, my native land.”
sentences.zh: 就在他死之前，他喊叫道：“我再也看不到我的祖国，我的家乡了。”

sentences.en: And now, many years after he had learned this poem, the reporter for the first time understood the sadness of the dying soldier.
sentences.zh: 如今，在他学会这首诗许多年之后，这位记者第一次理解了那名垂死士兵的悲伤。

sentences.en: Hours passed.
sentences.zh: 时间一分一秒地过去。

sentences.en: The reporter asked the sailor to take the oars so that he could rest.
sentences.zh: 记者请那名水手划桨，好让自己休息一下。

sentences.en: It seemed like only a brief period, but it was more than an hour later, when the sailor returned the oars to the reporter.
sentences.zh: 那似乎只过了很短的时间，可等水手把桨还给记者时，已经过去了一个多小时。

sentences.en: They both knew that only they could keep the boat from sinking.
sentences.zh: 他们都知道，只有他们才能防止小船沉没。

sentences.en: And so they rowed, hour after hour, through the night.
sentences.zh: 于是他们不停地划着桨，一个钟头又一个钟头，直到深夜。

sentences.en: When day came, the four men saw land again.
sentences.zh: 天亮了，那四个人又看到了陆地。

sentences.en: But there were no people on the shore.
sentences.zh: 但岸上却没有一个人。

sentences.en: A conference was held on the boat.
sentences.zh: 他们在船上召开了一次会议。

sentences.en: “Well,” said the captain, “if no help is coming, we might better try to reach the shore right away.
sentences.zh: “好吧，”船长说，“如果没有人来救援，我们不如赶紧想办法靠岸。

sentences.en: If we stay out here much longer, we will be too weak to do anything for ourselves at all.”
sentences.zh: 如果我们再在这里多待一会儿，我们就会虚弱得连自己都无能为力了。”

sentences.en: The others agreed.
sentences.zh: 其他人表示同意。

sentences.en: They began to turn the boat toward the beach.
sentences.zh: 他们开始把小船转向海滩。

sentences.en: The captain told them to be careful – that when the boat came near the beach, the waves would sink it.
sentences.zh: 船长叮嘱他们要小心——说小船靠近海滩时，海浪会把它打沉。

sentences.en: Then everyone should jump out of the boat and swim to the shore.
sentences.zh: 然后大家都应该跳出小船，游向岸边。

sentences.en: As the boat came closer to land, the waves got bigger and more violent.
sentences.zh: 随着小船离陆地越来越近，海浪变得越来越大，越来越汹涌。

sentences.en: At last, a large wave climbed into the air and fell on the small boat with great force.
sentences.zh: 最后，一道巨浪腾空而起，重重地砸在那艘小船上。

sentences.en: The boat turned over as the men jumped into the sea.
sentences.zh: 船翻了，男人们落入海中。

sentences.en: The water was like ice.
sentences.zh: 水冷得像冰一样。

sentences.en: The reporter was tired.
sentences.zh: 记者感到十分疲惫。

sentences.en: But he swam toward the beach.
sentences.zh: 但他仍朝海滩游去。

sentences.en: He looked for his friends.
sentences.zh: 他寻找着他的朋友们。

sentences.en: He saw Billie, the sailor, in front of him, swimming strongly and quickly.
sentences.zh: 他看见水手比利就在眼前，正奋力而迅速地游着。

sentences.en: The cook was near him.
sentences.zh: 厨师就在他附近。

sentences.en: Behind, the captain held on to the overturned boat with his one good hand.
sentences.zh: 在后面，船长用他那只有力的一只手紧抓住翻扣的船。

sentences.en: Soon, the reporter could swim no longer.
sentences.zh: 不一会儿，记者再也游不动了。

sentences.en: A current was carrying him back out to sea.
sentences.zh: 一股水流正把他向外海拖去。

sentences.en: He thought: “Am I going to drown?
sentences.zh: 他心想：“我要淹死了吗？

sentences.en: Can it be possible?”
sentences.zh: 这有可能吗？”

sentences.en: But the current suddenly changed and he was able to swim toward the shore.
sentences.zh: 然而水流突然改变，他得以朝岸边游去。

sentences.en: The captain called to him to swim to the boat and hold on.
sentences.zh: 船长喊他游向船只并抓住它。

sentences.en: The reporter started to swim toward the boat.
sentences.zh: 记者开始朝船游去。

sentences.en: Then he saw a man running along the shore.
sentences.zh: 接着，他看见一个男人在岸边奔跑。

sentences.en: He was quickly taking off his shoes and clothes.
sentences.zh: 他正迅速地脱下鞋子和衣服。

sentences.en: As the reporter got close to the boat, a large wave hit him and threw him into the air over the boat and far from it.
sentences.zh: 当记者靠近船只时，一道巨浪击中了他，把他抛向空中，越过船只，远远地抛到一旁。

sentences.en: When he tried to get up, he found that the water was not over his head, only half way up his body.
sentences.zh: 当他试图站起来时，他发现水并未没过他的头顶，只到他身体的一半。

sentences.en: But he was so tired that he could not stand up.
sentences.zh: 但他太累了，站不起来。

sentences.en: Each wave threw him down, and the current kept pulling him back to sea.
sentences.zh: 每一波浪都把他掀翻，水流不断把他往海里拖。

sentences.en: Then he saw the man again, jumping into the water.
sentences.zh: 然后他又看见那个人跳进水里。

sentences.en: The man pulled the cook to the shore.
sentences.zh: 那个人把厨师拉到岸边。

sentences.en: Then he ran back into the water for the captain.
sentences.zh: 然后他又跑回水里去救船长。

sentences.en: But the captain waved him away and sent him to the reporter.
sentences.zh: 但船长挥手让他离开，派他去救那位记者。

sentences.en: The man seized the reporter’s hand and pulled him to the beach.
sentences.zh: 那个人抓住记者的手，把他拉到海滩上。

sentences.en: Then the man pointed to the water and cried: “What’s that?”
sentences.zh: 然后那个人指向海水，喊道：“那是什么？”

sentences.en: In the shallow water, face down, lay Billie, the sailor.
sentences.zh: 在浅水区，脸朝下躺着的是水手比利。

sentences.en: The reporter did not know all that happened after that.
sentences.zh: 那位记者并不知道之后发生的一切。

sentences.en: He fell on the sand as if dropped from a housetop.
sentences.zh: 他摔在沙地上，仿佛从屋顶掉下来一般。

sentences.en: It seems that immediately the beach was filled with men with blankets, clothes and whiskey.
sentences.zh: 据说，海滩上立刻挤满了带着毛毯、衣服和威士忌的人。

sentences.en: Women brought hot coffee.
sentences.zh: 女人们端来热咖啡。

sentences.en: The people welcomed the men from the sea to the land.
sentences.zh: 人们把从海里救上来的男子迎接到陆地上。

sentences.en: But a still and dripping shape was carried slowly up the beach.
sentences.zh: 但一个静止的、滴着水的身影被缓缓抬上海滩。

sentences.en: And the land’s welcome for the sailor’s body could only be its final resting place.
sentences.zh: 而陆地对这位水尸的迎接，只能是他最后的安息之地。

sentences.en: When night came, the white waves moved in the moonlight.
sentences.zh: 当夜幕降临，白色的海浪在月光下起伏。

sentences.en: The wind brought the sound of the great sea’s voice to the men on the shore.​
sentences.zh: 风把大海那宏亮声音的声响带给岸上的人们。

glossary.def: a large and often dangerous sea fish with very sharp teeth
to move a boat through water using oars
